rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a multimodal fusion approach (combining RNA and image modalities) provides a meaningful accuracy advantage over single-modality baselines, and what a reasonable multimodal baseline achieves. config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) represents a well-motivated 'standard' multimodal setup: a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) captures cell-type structure, resnet50 provides a robust image representation, avgpool is a low-risk aggregation, and weighted fusion is a common, stable combination strategy. Testing this first establishes a reference accuracy from which all subsequent experiments (stronger encoders, transformer aggregation, alternative fusion, single-modality baselines) can be interpreted. If it performs well, we exploit by upgrading components; if it underperforms, we learn that multimodal fusion at this complexity level is insufficient and pivot toward single-modality or more expressive architectures. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-experiment budget.

With only one data point (config_001: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted → 67.8% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality actually contributes meaningful signal over RNA alone. config_002 is a clean single-variable ablation of config_001: it keeps the same RNA encoder (scvi_n200), profile setting (multiprofile), and aggregation (avgpool) but removes the image branch entirely. If rna_only matches or exceeds 67.8%, the remaining 8 experiments should pivot toward RNA-encoder and aggregation variants; if multimodal clearly wins, the budget should focus on optimizing image encoder, fusion, and aggregation within the multimodal family. Resolving this fundamental architectural question early maximizes the information value of the next 8 experiments and prevents wasting budget on multimodal refinements that may not be warranted.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.6776 acc, beating RNA-only config_002 (0.6501) by ~2.7%, confirming that the image modality contributes meaningfully. However, we have only tested ResNet50 as the image encoder. Question: Does upgrading to a stronger image encoder (ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L) further improve multimodal performance? config_008 is a clean single-variable change from config_001 (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l), isolating the effect of image encoder quality. Why this is the best next experiment: The image encoder is a high-impact design axis; ViT-L is substantially more expressive than ResNet50, and if the image branch is the bottleneck, this upgrade could yield the largest single gain available. Establishing whether ViT-L helps (or hurts) before further varying aggregation/fusion/RNA encoder ensures subsequent experiments build on the stronger backbone, making the remaining 7 experiments more efficient.

Evidence: config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the clear best at 0.7062 acc, and the comparison with config_001 (resnet50) shows imagenet_vit_l is the superior image encoder (+2.9pp). The comparison with config_002 confirms multimodal > rna_only. Question: Can upgrading the aggregation from avgpool to transformer further improve performance while retaining the proven weighted fusion and imagenet_vit_l encoder? config_041 isolates the aggregation variable (avgpool→transformer) on the best-known backbone, testing whether a more expressive cross-modal interaction mechanism (transformer) can capture richer feature interactions than simple average pooling. This is the best use of experiment 4 because it exploits the strongest evidence (imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion + scvi_n200) while probing the most impactful remaining design axis (aggregation), and with 6 experiments left, we should build incrementally on the proven best configuration rather than exploring orthogonal directions.

The current best (config_041: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250) was reached by sequentially improving the image encoder and aggregation method. The one remaining untested dimension within this exact setting is the fusion strategy: weighted vs. concat. Config_039 is a clean single-variable change (weighted → concat) from the current best, directly testing whether concatenation-based fusion captures complementary modality information better than weighted averaging. This is the highest-value next experiment because it either yields an immediate improvement to the best-known accuracy or confirms weighted fusion is optimal, thereby freeing the remaining 5 experiments to focus on the RNA encoder axis (scgpt, pca_n2000) without ambiguity about the fusion choice.

The current best (config_041, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted in a multiprofile multimodal setup. The image encoder, aggregation, and fusion choices are now well-supported by evidence (imagenet_vit_l > resnet50; transformer > avgpool; weighted ≈ concat). The major unexplored dimension is the RNA encoder: scgpt has not been tested in any configuration yet. Config_015 pairs scgpt with the proven-best image/aggregation/fusion stack, directly testing whether a more expressive learned RNA encoder (scgpt) can surpass scvi_n200 in the multimodal setting. This is the highest-value exploitation step: it keeps the architecture that already yields 0.725 and swaps only the RNA encoder, isolating that variable. With 4 experiments remaining, resolving the RNA encoder question now is critical before fine-tuning further.

The current best (config_041: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250) has been well-characterized across aggregation and fusion, but the RNA encoder dimension remains untested with this strong pipeline. config_015 showed scgpt is catastrophic (0.52), but pca_n2000 has never been paired with imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. Testing config_011 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) will clarify whether the RNA encoder is a critical bottleneck or whether the image encoder + transformer aggregation drive most of the performance. If PCA matches scvi_n200, it confirms the pipeline is robust and I can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning; if it falls well short, it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and I should exhaust scvi_n200 variants (e.g., singleprofile) in the last 3 experiments. This is the highest-information experiment given the sparse evidence on RNA encoder choice within the top-performing architecture.

The current best (config_041, 0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted in multiprofile mode. All top-performing configs are multiprofile, but we have no direct comparison of singleprofile with these best encoders. config_049 (multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted) tests whether the singleprofile architecture—using the two strongest encoders and the slightly preferred weighted fusion—can match or exceed the multiprofile result. This is the highest-value remaining question: if singleprofile is competitive, it opens a new optimization axis for the final 2 experiments; if not, it confirms multiprofile as the correct architecture and lets us focus remaining budget on fine-grained variations around config_041. No other untested config with scvi_n200+vit_l offers a more informative architectural test.

The current best (config_041: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) is well-supported by strong evidence across RNA encoder, image encoder, profile, and model setting choices. The remaining uncertainty is in the aggregation×fusion interaction: we have transformer+weighted (0.725), transformer+concat (0.721), and avgpool+weighted (0.706), but avgpool+concat is untested. Config_044 completes this 2×2 grid for the best encoder pair, clarifying whether any fusion/aggregation combination could rival or exceed the current best. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, confirming (or potentially surprising) the optimal aggregation-fusion pairing is the highest-information use of this slot, directly informing the final experiment's choice.

The best result so far is config_041 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) at 0.725. All four aggregation×fusion combinations for that exact encoder pair have been tested. The strongest untested direction is to keep the proven best components (scvi_n200, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile) while substituting resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l (config_022). Evidence shows resnet50 trails imagenet_vit_l by ~0.028 with avgpool+weighted (0.678 vs 0.706), but the transformer aggregation added ~0.019 on top of avgpool with imagenet_vit_l, so config_022 is expected around 0.69–0.71. Among all untested configurations, this has the highest expected accuracy because it retains the three strongest factors (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion) and only changes the image backbone. As the final experiment, this maximizes the probability of either confirming the robustness of the transformer+weighted design or discovering a marginally better result, while all other untested options (scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, rna_only, image_only) are strongly indicated by prior evidence to underperform.
